blocks.x: One of the most influential film noir classics ever made is streaming for free this month as part of the soft-launch of a brand-new platform that is slated to launch in earnest in October. The movie in question is considered a major inspiration behind the French New Wave, and has influenced directors such as Quentin Tarantino and Jean-Luc Godard. Interestingly, it is widely believed that the briefcase MacGuffin in Tarantino’s Pulp Fiction was directly inspired by a similar object in the film noir classic, although Tarantino has downplayed the overlap as mostly coincidental. He has, however, admitted that the movie in question inspired Bruce Willis’ character in Pulp Fiction.

The classic was released in 1955 and directed by Robert Aldrich. Starring Ralph Meeker as a private investigator who becomes embroiled in a mystery after picking up a female hitchhiker, the movie notably marked the feature film debut of Cloris Leachman. The movie wasn’t very successful in its initial release, which was further hampered by criticism aimed at its themes and characters. Committees claimed that the movie would be a negative influence on the youth. Tarantino was certainly influenced by it; he went on to say years later in an interview, “I wanted Butch to be a complete f***ing a**hole. I wanted him to be basically like Ralph Meeker as Mike Hammer in Aldrich's movie. I wanted him to be a bully and a jerk, except that when he's with his girlfriend, Fabienne, he's a sweetheart.”

It is one of the most formally controlled films ever made, and its controlled restraint is what makes it so terrifying. You want your films to haunt you, not comfort you.
